passage.text: Rogers called this the actualizing tendency, a universal human motivation that leads to growth, development, and individual autonomy. He argued that the actualizing tendency was the single natural motivational force in human beings, and that it is always directed toward constructive growth. Furthermore, Rogers suggested that this process happens automatically when the social environment is optimal.

source.title: How Humanistic Is Positive Psychology? Lessons in Positive Psychology From Carl Rogers

taps.correct: Furthermore, Rogers suggested that this process happens automatically when the social environment is optimal.
wrong: Furthermore, Rogers proved that this process always happens automatically when the social environment is optimal.
taps.explain: The word 'suggested' softens the claim; it indicates an idea rather than a proven fact.

taps.context: He argued that the actualizing tendency was the single natural motivational force in human beings, and that it is always directed toward constructive growth.
taps.explain: The pronoun 'it' refers back to the subject of the sentence: the actualizing tendency.

taps.prompt: What is the main idea of the text?
taps.correct: Rogers believed that humans have one natural drive for growth that works best in supportive environments.
wrong: Rogers claimed that social environments create the human motivation to grow and develop.
Rogers argued that constructive growth only occurs when people choose to pursue autonomy deliberately.
taps.explain: The excerpt focuses on an innate tendency and optimal conditions, not environment as a cause.
